TARROW COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS
REGULAR SESSION AGENDA
Tuesday, October 13, 2026, 9:30 a.m.
Commissioners' Chambers, Tarrow County Administration Building, 41 Court Street, Tarrow City
Posted October 6, 2026
1. Call to order and Pledge of Allegiance
2. Roll call
3. Public comment (three minutes per speaker; please sign in at the door)
4. Approval of minutes: regular session of October 6, 2026
5. Consent agenda
a. Then-and-now certificates, County Auditor
b. Road maintenance agreement with Wrenfield Township for the Kessler Road culvert
6. County Engineer: award of bid for the 2026 crack-seal program
7. Resolution 2026-118: Moratorium on battery energy storage facility zoning applications (summary
on page 2)
8. Resolution 2026-119: Appropriation transfer, Sheriff's Office
9. Executive session, if needed
10. Adjourn
[Page 2]
Page 2 of 2
Item 7: Resolution 2026-118
A resolution declaring a moratorium on the acceptance and processing of applications for zoning
permits, zoning map amendments and conditional use approvals for battery energy storage facilities in
the unincorporated areas subject to the Tarrow County Zoning Resolution, and directing the Tarrow
County Zoning Commission to study the matter and recommend amendments.
Summary prepared by the Clerk of the Board
Duration: Twelve (12) months from the effective date, unless ended earlier by resolution of the Board.
Applies to: New applications for battery energy storage facilities with a rated capacity of one (1)
megawatt or more.
Applies in: The unincorporated areas subject to the Tarrow County Zoning Resolution (currently
Ferris, Quill and Brindle townships). Townships that administer their own zoning are not affected.
Does not apply to: Applications filed and determined to be complete before the effective date; battery
systems that serve a single home or business on the same property.
Effective date: Immediately upon adoption.
Study: The Zoning Commission is directed to recommend setback, fire-safety and decommissioning
standards to the Board within nine (9) months.

Page 1 of 1
WRENFIELD TOWNSHIP
Tarrow County, Ohio
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
Zoning Text Amendment ZTA-2026-03: Battery Energy Storage Systems
The Wrenfield Township Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing on Wednesday, October 21,
2026, at 7:00 p.m. at the Wrenfield Township Hall, 8 Gable Road, on proposed amendments to the
Wrenfield Township Zoning Resolution.
The proposed amendments would:
1. Add definitions of "battery energy storage system" and "battery energy storage facility".
2. Allow battery energy storage facilities as a conditional use in the I-1 Light Industrial District only.
3. Require a setback of at least 300 feet from any existing dwelling and at least 100 feet from any
property line.
4. Require a decommissioning plan and a financial guarantee (bond or letter of credit) covering
removal costs, to be reviewed every five years.
5. Require a fire-safety plan reviewed by the Fire Chief before a zoning certificate is issued.
The proposed text may be inspected at the Township Hall during office hours and on the township
website. Written comments may be submitted to the Zoning Inspector until 4:00 p.m. on Friday,
October 16, 2026. After the hearing, the Zoning Commission will send its recommendation to the
Board of Township Trustees.
By order of the Wrenfield Township Zoning Commission. Posted October 5, 2026.

excerpt: [Page 1]

CITY OF MARLOWE FALLS, OHIO
ORDINANCE NO. 2026-41
As amended in the Safety Committee, October 5, 2026
AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING FIRE SAFETY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE
REQUIREMENTS FOR BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS.
Section 1. Applicability. This ordinance applies to battery energy storage systems with an aggregate
energy capacity greater than 600 kWh, other than systems serving a single one- or two-family
dwelling.
Section 2. Standards. Systems shall be designed, installed and maintained in accordance with NFPA
855, Standard for the Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems, in the edition in effect when
the permit application is filed.
Section 3. Emergency response plan. Before a certificate of occupancy is issued, the owner shall
submit an emergency response plan approved by the Fire Chief.
Section 4. Annual walkthrough. The owner shall host a site walkthrough with the Marlowe Falls Fire
Department once each calendar year.
Section 5. Signs and contacts. A 24-hour emergency contact number shall be posted at each entrance
to the site.
Section 6. Effective date. This ordinance takes effect at the earliest date allowed by law.
[Page 2]
Page 2 of 2
Safety Committee amendments, October 5, 2026
1. Section 1: threshold raised from 50 kWh to 600 kWh.
2. Section 4: walkthrough changed from twice each year to once each calendar year.
First reading: September 21, 2026. Second reading: October 19, 2026.
